claims.text: Multiphase alloys with specific chemical-ordering tendencies will undergo a ductile-brittle-ductile transition during aging.
The non-monotonic ductility transition is driven by competition between precipitate hardening and precipitate coarsening or over-aging.
The proposed initial material is an as-quenched or solution-treated multiphase alloy containing solutes capable of forming ordered precipitates.
Isothermal aging at the proposed temperature induces precipitation and chemical ordering.
The relevant aging temperature is below the precipitate solvus.
The relevant aging temperature is above the ordering temperature.
The aging interval spans precipitate nucleation through precipitate coarsening.
Aging changes precipitate volume fraction.
Aging changes precipitate size.
Aging changes the degree of precipitate chemical ordering, potentially producing L12 or B2 ordered phases.
Initial aging increases alloy strength.
Initial aging reduces alloy ductility.
Coherent ordered precipitates impede dislocation motion.
Further aging causes precipitate coarsening.
Further aging causes a loss of precipitate coherency or ordering.
Coarsening and loss of coherency or ordering reduce the barrier to dislocation glide.
The reduced barrier to dislocation glide during over-aging restores ductility.
Ductility versus aging time follows a U-shaped or V-shaped curve.
The ductility minimum coincides with the peak-hardness or maximally ordered state.
The transition is restricted to alloys whose ordered precipitate structure significantly changes the slip mechanism and may be absent with disordered precipitates or an inherently brittle matrix.

contradictions.description: The intervention is said to induce and increase chemical ordering, but the aging temperature is specified as above the ordering temperature. If 'ordering temperature' means the equilibrium order-disorder transition temperature, ordering is normally favored below it, so the stated temperature boundary conflicts with the proposed mediator unless a different kinetic threshold is intended.
